Can You Appraise a House Without Stepping Inside? Sometimes, Yes.

What if you need a home appraisal but coordinating an interior visit is difficult?

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

When a desktop approach may be an optionDesktop does not mean automaticStart with who will rely on the reportMore in Appraisal Guides ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

If you need a valuation for an estate, divorce, financial planning, or another private matter, begin with the purpose of the appraisal and who will rely on it. A court, attorney, lender, or other intended user may require a particular report or inspection scope.

When a desktop approach may be an option

What if you need a home appraisal but coordinating an interior visit is difficult? A desktop appraisal may be an option. Rather than relying on a new in-person interior inspection, the appraiser develops an opinion of value using available property records, market data, photographs, prior documentation, and other credible sources. It can be a practical solution for certain private-use assignments.

Desktop does not mean automatic

But “desktop” does not mean “automatic.” A qualified appraiser still analyzes comparable sales, property characteristics, market conditions, and the reliability of the information provided. The tradeoff is that some important details, especially current interior condition or undocumented improvements, may be harder to verify. That is why a desktop approach is not appropriate for every property or intended use.

Start with who will rely on the report

If you need a valuation for an estate, divorce, financial planning, or another private matter, begin with the purpose of the appraisal and who will rely on it. A court, attorney, lender, or other intended user may require a particular report or inspection scope. Reddy Appraisal LLC can discuss whether a desktop residential appraisal is suitable or whether an interior inspection would be the better choice.

About this article

General educational information. The suitable appraisal scope depends on the property, intended use, effective date and available information.
